title: Flower Stamp (make your own command)
body:
Goal: use def to make a new command, flower(x, y, color), then use it to stamp flowers all over the screen.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run (F5). Nothing is drawn! Read the code: the recipe def flower(x, y): is there, but nobody ever calls it. (That is this week's bug hunt.)
  2. At the bottom, call it three times, e.g. flower(-200, 0). Run it.
  3. All the flowers are orange. Give the recipe a third parameter: change the first line to def flower(x, y, color): and change t.color("#E69F00") to t.color(color).
  4. Now each call needs a color too: flower(-200, 0, PALETTE[0]), flower(0, 0, PALETTE[6]), flower(200, 0, PALETTE[4]).

Done looks like: at least 3 flowers, in at least 2 different colors, each with a yellow middle.

Extra: add a size parameter and use t.circle(size) for the petals. Or make a meadow: call flower 10 times!

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the bottom of starter.py. The recipe called flower is written, but nothing ever uses it, so the screen stays empty. Making a recipe and using it are two different jobs.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: To use a recipe, write its name followed by parentheses with the values inside. Each call puts a flower in a new spot. For colors, give the recipe a third slot in its first line, and use that slot instead of the fixed color inside.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: A call looks like flower(____, ____, PALETTE[____]). The first two blanks are where the middle goes. The last is a spot in the list, counting from 0. The recipe's first line needs color added, and t.color( ) needs to use it.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Flower Stamp - make your own command with def

import turtle

# The color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.speed(0)
t.hideturtle()


# A new command! flower(x, y) draws a flower with its middle at x, y.
# The lines pushed in under def are the RECIPE. They only run when we CALL it.
# TODO: add a third parameter called color, and use it in t.color(...)
def flower(x, y):
    t.penup()
    t.goto(x, y)
    t.pendown()
    t.color("#E69F00")
    for petal in range(6):
        t.begin_fill()
        t.circle(25)
        t.end_fill()
        t.left(60)
    t.dot(20, "#F0E442")    # the yellow middle


# TODO: call flower three times at different places, for example:
#   flower(-200, 0)

turtle.done()
